newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan life insurers' outlook negative -- Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Japan life insurers' outlook negative -- Moody's.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Friday that the rating outlook for Japanese life insurers was negative, with competitiveness declining in the face of their large portfolios of low-yielding stocks, inefficient distribution and high and rigid cost structures.

"If the Nikkei share average is at 18,000, the stock portfolios of almost all companies, with the exception of Nippon Life Insurance, Dai-ichi Mutual Life Insurance, Meiji Mutual Life Insurance and several medium-sized companies, are under water," Moody's said.
In fact, even at higher levels of the Nikkei, some insurers no longer have undervalued securities that could be marked to market to adjust profitability, it said.

If they are forced to recognise unrealised losses at the end of the business year on March 31 they will become insolvent, it said, adding that since these life insurers are mutual companies and do not have equity, a fiscal year net losss represents insolvency.
